title: At al-Ukhaydir the Mamlūk army, 9,408 strong, attacks 2,368 of the Banū Lām and beats them: 1,508 lost against 243

data.note: a battle of the Mamlūks' war; al-Andalus is in it as an ally and has not fought

title: The ideas of the far voyages take root: al-Andalus embraces the New World among its institutions, with no new land found, only the ways of thinking that exploration has brought

data.trent: no discovery- just the entrenchment of exploration ideals

title: A grandson for the prince Aḥmad: Aḥmad, son of his son Muḥammad

data.others: also born in 1451: Zaynab (30 January) and Muʾmina (26 December 1450) to Saʿd ibn Aḥmad of Banbalūna, the first by the prince Aḥmad's daughter Muʾmina

title: A second idea wins the court: instead of a new ṭāʾifa, Sicily is kept under the crown, with a governor at Palermo, for now

data.trent: It's go towards the crown, for now.
data.save: Sicily's 22 towns are still held directly in December 1451; no new subject

source: Trent's account (12 November 2026); save of 21 December 1451

title: The treasury, 2,812 at the start of the year, is spent down to 26: new paper mills at Ishbīliya, al-Mariyya, Shāṭiba and Shantarīn, jewellers at Qurṭuba, Jayyān and Sharīsh, a library at al-Ushbūna, a quarry at Palermo, and paved roads

data.also: a cannon foundry at Jaén, lumber mills at Córdoba and Messina, a weapons guild at Murcia, cloth at Badajoz
data.roads: paved roads under way in November 1451 (Trent's screenshot)
data.stability: 23.6 in February, 16.1 in December; the save doesn't say why
